title: Quantum reference frames beyond subsystems: a reconstruction and generalization of the perspective-neutral framework
locators: Abstract; Sec. IV.3; Example 29 and Eqs. (39)-(57); Appendix B.1 Eqs. (53)-(57); Appendix B.2 Example 32 Eqs. (58)-(59); references [97], [99]-[102]
assumptions: Main formal construction assumes finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and compact Lie symmetry groups (Sec. II, lines 90-91); continuous R example 29 is explicitly outside the framework and omits correct normalization (Sec. IV.3, lines 747-751). Finite Abelian Z_n example is stated as rigorous. Constraint includes interaction; ordinary subsystem clock states generated by H_C differ from full constraint. Non-local center-of-mass instrument frame recovers a factorized relative-coordinate evolution for the specific translation-plus-K(X1-X2)^2 model.
conclusion: Authors generalize perspective-neutral QRFs to covariant instruments not tied to tensor-factor subsystems; derive exact relational Schrödinger dynamics with interactions in cited clock examples and a finite Abelian analogue. Does not assert arbitrary interactions admit decoupling/autonomous evolution; generalized formalism permits treating interactions without claiming dynamics/ontology are changed by representation alone.
proof_status: Primary HTML full text inspected. Formal claims/equations read at stated locators, not independently proved or reproduced.
dependencies: Relies on the perspective-neutral QRF framework, compact-group representations, covariant operations/instruments; cites Smith & Ahmadi (2019), Höhn et al. (2021), and relational clock-switching work.
open_questions: Which non-local clock instruments yield autonomous reduced dynamics for interactions outside the commuting relative-potential example? How are operational probabilities compared across subsystem and non-subsystem frames? No novelty claim without citation forward check.
relevance: Directly narrows interaction and non-subsystem QRF gaps; key recent predecessor.
limits: Abstract and selected full-text sections inspected; not all general formal proofs audited. Example 29's continuous R model omits correct normalization; Example 32 is finite Abelian and model-specific. No independent reproduction.

title: The Trinity of Relational Quantum Dynamics
locators: Sec. II.2 Eq. (4); Sec. III.2 Eqs. (13)-(20), especially (15)-(16); Sec. IV.1 Eq. (27), Theorems 1-2; Sec. V Theorems 3-6; Appendix A; Sec. IX conclusion
assumptions: Global clock/system phase-space partition, clock phase-space dimension 2, autonomous constraint C_H=H_C+H_S≈0 with no clock-system interaction; one Hamiltonian constraint; covariant clock POVM density proportional to rank-one (possibly generalized) |t><t| effects and normalized resolution; clock Hamiltonian spectral cases developed for non-degenerate continuous/discrete spectra, with degeneracy/periodicity via cited extensions. Physical system subspace selected by constraint projection Π_sigmaSC.
conclusion: Three descriptions (relational Dirac observables, Page-Wootters conditional Schrödinger, quantum symmetry-reduced relational Heisenberg) are equivalent under stated uncoupled model hypotheses. Covariant POVMs accommodate bounded/non-ideal clocks, nonorthogonal and overcomplete time states, and resolve the monotonicity problem; no ideal/self-adjoint time operator is required. Appendix A and conclusion explicitly identify clock-system interactions as a major open extension for generic models; certain interactions already modify PW evolution in cited work.
proof_status: Primary HTML full text inspected; equations and stated theorem locators read. Proofs not independently reconstructed or checked beyond paper text.
dependencies: Dirac constraint quantization/group averaging, covariant POVMs, reduction maps; appendix discussion cites interaction-free factorization and prior interaction work.
open_questions: How do the trinity reduction maps generalize when the clock couples to S and/or only an instrument on a non-subsystem defines the clock? Need compare existing interaction and non-local-frame constructions before claiming open status.
relevance: Essential predecessor; already covers broad non-ideal clock POVMs, while uncoupled hypothesis bounds its equivalence claim.
limits: Formal proof correspondence not independently audited; extension to generic interacting systems is not supplied by the central theorem.

title: Equivalence of approaches to relational quantum dynamics in relativistic settings
version: arXiv:2007.00580v1; journal Frontiers in Physics 9 (2021), DOI 10.3389/fphy.2021.587083
locators: Sec. II constraint Eq. (13); Sec. III frequency sectors Eqs. (10)-(12); Sec. IV.2 clock POVM Eqs. (25)-(30), Lemmas 1-3; Sec. V.1 Theorems 1-2; Sec. V.3 Theorems 4-5
assumptions: Uncoupled clock/system split; quadratic clock Hamiltonian H_C=s p_t^2/2, s=±1, giving C_H=s p_t^2/2+H_S≈0 (Eq. 10); frequency label sigma=± and sectorwise reduction. Clock time POVM uses nonorthogonal overcomplete sector states; group averaging/physical inner product and sectorwise reductions. Reduced phase-space quantization is not always equivalent unless an extra condition holds.
conclusion: Extends equivalence sector by sector to quadratic relativistic clock constraints, with covariant POVM and normalized conditioning on time plus frequency; includes relativistic particle and homogeneous cosmology examples. It does not remove the two frequency branches or make cross-sector clock change automatically invertible; frame maps are restricted to sector overlaps.

relevance: Closes a broad 'relativistic clocks/frequency branches' gap; exact sector restrictions are important.
limits: Selected full text read; imported theorem proofs not rebuilt. No empirical or ontological inference.

title: Measurement events relative to temporal quantum reference frames
locators: Sec. 2 clock model Eq. (2); Sec. 4.1-4.2 Eqs. (15)-(22); Sec. 4.2.3 Eqs. (21)-(22); Appendix E Eqs. (76)-(82); Sec. 5 discrete-time model
assumptions: Clock C with Hilbert space L²[-E,E] and bounded clock energy; TO approach uses covariant/twirled observables and external measurement protocol; PM approach adds ancilla A and clock-triggered interaction K_SA(t) in the constraint. Distinguishes perfect orthogonal clock limit E→∞ from finite-spectrum nonideal clock; finite overlap of clock states causes memory kernel/nonlocality.
conclusion: TO and PM approaches agree for multi-time predictions with ideal clocks but model different operational event notions. In nonideal PM, conditioned dynamics is generally time-nonlocal and may be nonunitary; measurement terms can contribute in both orders for disjoint supports. A finite/discrete-time construction can recover unitarity for general measurement interactions. This is an author/model claim, not evidence that fundamental time is discrete or physical causal order is indefinite.

dependencies: Page-Wootters; Höhn et al. clock-neutral observables; Smith-Ahmadi interaction kernel; quantum measurement ancilla model.

relevance: A fully inspected nearby result shows clock nonideality plus clock-triggered interaction effects, sharpening any equivalence extension.
limits: No independent reproduction; claims are model-specific; finite clock-spectrum effects do not establish fundamental temporal discreteness or ontological indeterminism. title: Quantizing time: Interacting clocks and systems
assumptions: Tensor-factor clock C/system S, interacting Hamiltonian constraint H=H_C+H_S+H_int; clock states generated by H_C and resolution of identity, with ideal orthogonal clock for examples 1-2 and finite-dimensional periodic qubit clock in example 3. Authors choose physical inner product conditional on clock projector and require time-independent normalization; interaction is self-adjoint.
conclusion: Conditional system state obeys i d/dt psi_S=H_S psi_S+integral K(t,t')psi_S(t')dt', K=<t|H_int|t'>; norm/isometry condition follows from chosen physical inner product being time-independent. Perturbative Dyson-like series and gravity/qubit examples supplied. It does not prove the 2019 trinity equivalence for interacting POVM clocks.
proof_status: Primary HTML full text inspected; exact kernel, norm condition, and examples read. Calculations not independently reproduced.
dependencies: Page-Wootters conditional probability interpretation; Dirac constraint quantization; selected physical inner product.
open_questions: What is the equivalent Dirac-observable/relational-Heisenberg description under interaction for general covariant POVM clocks, and when is conditioning an isometry under a physical inner product compatible with measurable clock effects? limits: Specific conditional construction and clock classes; physical inner product is a stated choice; no full generalization of the trinity or ontology result.
